headline: Ross comps jumped 10% on traffic, a second straight double-digit quarter; EPS and full-year outlook raised.
guidance_note: FY26 EPS raised to $8.61-8.77 incl. ~$0.60 tariff refunds. Q3 comp +6-7%, EPS $1.75-1.83; Q4 comp +4-5%.
key_messages: Comp +10%, driven mainly by more customer traffic: new shoppers, lapsed customers returning, and more frequent trips; July strongest month.
Reported EPS $2.66 includes ~$0.60 from ~$253m IEEPA tariff refunds; ex-refunds op margin still +205 bps.
Merchandise margin +110 bps; inventories +18% with packaway 36% of total vs 38% LY.
CEO Conroy: Ross has outgrown its two major rivals for four quarters, 'mathematically we've captured more share'.
Department store weakness and retail order cancellations are feeding off-price supply; higher fuel-driven freight a Q3 headwind.

consumer.income_split: Traffic gains broad across demographics, per management.
consumer.pricing: Expects modest low-single-digit average unit retail increases in 2H; tariff refunds boosted Q2 profit.
consumer.quote: We achieved stellar sales and earnings growth in the second quarter.

macro_read: Double-digit, traffic-led comps at a low-price apparel chain show strong demand for value and share shift from department stores.
